claims.claim: FastAPI recognizes Pydantic model-typed parameters as JSON request bodies and validates inputs.
claims.notes: The demo lacks production authentication and rate limiting.

claims.claim: FastAPI lifespan handlers provide startup/shutdown resource management; async routes do not automatically make CPU-bound model inference nonblocking.
claims.notes: The example uses synchronous def endpoints for CPU-bound toy inference.

claims.claim: Pickle/joblib model loading can execute arbitrary code, and cross-version scikit-learn model persistence is not guaranteed.
claims.notes: Load only trusted artifacts in controlled environments; consider skops.io threat model.

claims.claim: ONNX Runtime runs exported graphs with declared providers and needs parity verification of names, shapes, classes and numerical tolerance.
claims.notes: No guaranteed speedup from converting a model to ONNX; target hardware benchmarks needed.

claims.claim: P95 is an empirical quantile of end-to-end request latency and is not in general a sum of each component's P95.
claims.notes: Synthetic latency histogram/budget is explicitly illustrative, not production data.

claims.claim: Canary release routes a small portion of traffic to a candidate and evaluates observable risk before traffic expansion.
claims.notes: 95/5 split and thresholds shown are invented examples, not universal release standards.

claims.claim: Covariate shift in P(X) and concept drift in P(Y|X) are different notions; reliable model-performance assessment generally requires labels.
claims.locator: Model dependency risk and system drift background
claims.notes: Definitions are mathematical; the chapter explicitly notes immature labels and source selection.

claims.claim: The Dockerfile is an illustrative build recipe, not a built or scanned production image.
claims.notes: Production should pin image digest and dependency hashes; no deployment is claimed.
